selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main claim made about the person carrying the decree?
questions.answer: He is completely truthful and cannot be accused of lying.

questions.question: What is the “decree” in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the Qur’an.

questions.question: From whom does this decree come?
questions.answer: It comes from the Lord and Creator of the universe.

questions.question: What detail shows how widely this decree has been received over time?
questions.answer: In every century, more than three hundred million people have accepted and confirmed it.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the special nature of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an is amazing in seven ways and has many signs of being beyond human ability.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do those signs prove about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They prove that it is the speech of the Creator of all beings.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention another treatise instead of giving a full explanation here?
questions.answer: Because that work already explains the proofs in detail, so this passage moves on briefly.

questions.question: What does the traveller conclude from the Prophet’s role as messenger of the decree?
questions.answer: He concludes that the Prophet would never betray the message by lying.

questions.question: Why would lying be especially impossible for the one delivering this message?
questions.answer: Because lying would go against the message itself and would be disloyal to the One who sent it.

questions.question: What relationship between the messenger and the message strengthens the argument in this passage?
questions.answer: The messenger is presented as faithfully announcing a divine revelation, so his honesty is tied to the truth of what he carries.

questions.question: What central idea does this passage try to prove about the Prophet?
questions.answer: It tries to prove that he is truthful and free from falsehood.

questions.question: What object in his hand is used as evidence for that truthfulness?
questions.answer: The Qur’an, described as a decree.

questions.question: How is the source of that decree presented?
questions.answer: It is presented as coming from the Lord of the universe.

questions.question: What does the repeated acceptance of the decree in every century suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the message has lasting authority and broad recognition across time.

questions.question: According to the passage, how many broad ways is the Qur’an described as extraordinary?
questions.answer: Seven broad ways.

questions.question: What additional point is made about the Qur’an’s miraculous character?
questions.answer: It is said to have forty aspects that show its miraculous nature.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from those miraculous qualities?
questions.answer: That the Qur’an is the word of the Creator, not a human product.

questions.question: How does the passage use outside scholarship or earlier writing?
questions.answer: It refers readers to another well-known work where these proofs are explained with strong evidence.

questions.question: What moral failure would lying involve for the one who delivers this decree?
questions.answer: It would be both a betrayal of the decree and an act of unfaithfulness toward Allah.

questions.question: What can we infer about the messenger’s duty from this passage?
questions.answer: His duty is to deliver the revelation honestly and exactly as he received it.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the Qur’an compared to in terms of authority?
questions.answer: It is compared to an official command or decree.

questions.question: Why is that comparison important for understanding the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that the Qur’an is not presented as an ordinary book but as a message carrying divine authority.

questions.question: How does the passage show that this decree has a strong historical impact?
questions.answer: It says huge numbers of people in every century have accepted and affirmed it.

questions.question: What does the title given to the Qur’an suggest about its rank?
questions.answer: It suggests greatness, honor, and a very high status.
